final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 in TM10 is the primary organic cation-coordinating carboxylate in OCT1; isosteric D473N neutralizes the essential negative charge to abolish transport while preserving local TM packing and folding.
E454 provides an essential electrostatic interaction along the translocation pore; E454Q neutralizes the charge to eliminate transport while retaining side-chain bulk and helix stability.
D473A ablates the critical negative charge required for cation recognition, completely knocking out transport activity while being well-tolerated within the TM helix.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations targeting key active-site electrostatic residues are well established to abolish transport while preserving folding, rendering further evidence collection unnecessary.

history.rationale: D473 is the canonical substrate-coordinating acidic residue in the central binding cavity; neutralization to Asn abolishes cation transport while preserving side-chain volume and local hydrogen-bonding network to maintain folding.
AlphaMissense classifies D473N as pathogenic (LOF proxy 0.589), supporting loss of transport, while the isosteric carboxamide preserves local folding.
D473A removes the essential carboxylate that anchors organic cations, severely impairing substrate transport while retaining structural compatibility within TM10.
Strong pathogenic prediction (0.803) aligns with known functional ablation of the key cation-coordinating TM10 aspartate.
W216 provides critical aromatic and cation-pi interactions in the binding pocket; alanine substitution disrupts substrate coordination without destabilizing the transmembrane bundle.
Pathogenicity score of 0.635 supports ablation of substrate aromatic stacking in the central cavity.
E454 lines the translocation cleft; isosteric substitution to Gln removes the negative charge necessary for substrate permeation while preserving helical packing.
High pathogenicity score (0.776) indicates transport disruption, and the isosteric substitution minimizes disruption to TM folding.
E454A eliminates an active-cleft acidic group essential for organic cation translocation, substantially decreasing transport activity.
High pathogenicity (0.881) confirms transport loss, though alanine removal of side-chain volume may affect stability slightly more than glutamine.
W216F alters the precise steric and electrostatic profile of the primary cavity Trp, reducing transport efficiency while fully supporting native-like helical stability.
Low pathogenicity score (0.264) indicates that aromatic substitution F is functionally tolerated and likely retains transport activity.
F160 lines the substrate translocation pathway in TM2; truncation to alanine impairs hydrophobic interactions with organic cations.
Lowest pathogenicity score (0.127), strongly suggesting retention of wild-type transport capability.
R487 participates in intracellular gating and salt-bridge networks involved in the transport cycle; alanine mutation disrupts alternating-access dynamics.
Low pathogenicity (0.168) indicates transport function is likely retained.
D397 is a conserved polar/charged residue in TM7; neutralization to Asn disrupts functional charge interactions during transport while maintaining membrane insertion.
Predicted benign (0.260), indicating weak impact on OCT1 transport function.
C472 is adjacent to the catalytic D473 in the pore lining; alanine substitution alters local pore geometry and substrate accessibility without causing misfolding.
Low-to-moderate pathogenicity (0.323) suggests C472 substitution may not reliably abolish substrate translocation.
